text: The coordinate quotient equivalence sends [(x,y)] to ([x],[y]), and the half-norm splits as B_L(x,x)/2+B_M(y,y)/2. Thus it preserves the whole quadratic map, exactly the orthogonal-sum formula in [Nikulin §1.3](https://www.mathnet.ru/php/getFT.phtml?jrnid=im&option_lang=eng&paperid=1677&what=fullteng#page=7), after converting ℚ/2ℤ to the half-norm ℚ/ℤ convention. Evenness and nondegeneracy of both lattices are explicit. Published [control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/IntegralLattice/Discriminant/Operations.lean#L283) passes, [control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/IntegralLattice/Discriminant/Operations.lean#L294) passes.
The isometry uses componentwise quotient representatives.
Its polar isometry agrees with the bilinear construction.

The dual of a product carrier for the orthogonal sum is the product of duals, and quotienting by L×M yields A_L×A_M. This is the canonical discriminant-group decomposition in [Dolgachev §1.2](https://sites.lsa.umich.edu/idolga-new/wp-content/uploads/sites/1467/2024/08/bourbaki83.pdf#page=4). The explicit quotient equivalence also works for degenerate forms; no finiteness is asserted there. Published [control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/IntegralLattice/Discriminant/Operations.lean#L148) passes, [control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/Quotient/Prod.lean#L105) passes.
The quotient map uses the two component classes.
Its inverse assembles a pair of representatives.

Forgetting the quadratic structure leaves precisely the constructed coordinate quotient equivalence. This identifies the underlying map in [Nikulin §1.3](https://www.mathnet.ru/php/getFT.phtml?jrnid=im&option_lang=eng&paperid=1677&what=fullteng#page=7)’s orthogonal-sum formula. The equality is between additive equivalences, retaining all representative data; it does not identify different quotient types by equality. Published [control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/IntegralLattice/Discriminant/Operations.lean#L271) passes.
Evaluation agrees with the canonical quotient equivalence.

Pairing integrally with every (l,m) is equivalent to pairing integrally with every l and every m: test (l,0) and (0,m), then add. This is the dual-lattice calculation behind [Dolgachev §1.2](https://sites.lsa.umich.edu/idolga-new/wp-content/uploads/sites/1467/2024/08/bourbaki83.pdf#page=4)’s discriminant-sum formula. It requires no nondegeneracy or positivity. Published [control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/IntegralLattice/Discriminant/Operations.lean#L87) passes.
The elementwise criterion gives equality of embedded dual carriers.

The inverse dual-carrier equivalence joins its two dual vectors into their original ambient pair. Componentwise integral pairing proves membership, and both coordinate projections recover the input. This is the explicit inverse underlying the canonical decomposition in [Dolgachev §1.2](https://sites.lsa.umich.edu/idolga-new/wp-content/uploads/sites/1467/2024/08/bourbaki83.pdf#page=4); it uses no basis or representative choice. Published [control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/IntegralLattice/Discriminant/Operations.lean#L107) passes.
The forward map recovers the two original coordinates.

The canonical quotient equivalence takes a dual representative (x,y) to its two classes [x] and [y]. Mapping the original product carrier to the product of embedded carriers makes this independent of the representative. This is exactly the quotient decomposition of [Dolgachev §1.2](https://sites.lsa.umich.edu/idolga-new/wp-content/uploads/sites/1467/2024/08/bourbaki83.pdf#page=4). Published [control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/IntegralLattice/Discriminant/Operations.lean#L283) passes.
The quadratic isometry retains the same representative formula.

Negating B preserves the dual and original carrier, so the quotient map is the identity on representatives. Its half-norm becomes −B(x,x)/2, giving an isometry to the negated quadratic module, directly from [Nikulin §1.3](https://www.mathnet.ru/php/getFT.phtml?jrnid=im&option_lang=eng&paperid=1677&what=fullteng#page=7)’s defining formula. The target negates q as well as its polar pairing. Published [control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/IntegralLattice/Discriminant/Operations.lean#L469) passes, [control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/IntegralLattice/Discriminant/Operations.lean#L477) passes.
The isometry keeps each ambient representative.
Its polar isometry is the corresponding bilinear negation.

Under coordinate splitting, an original lattice vector in L⊕M has first coordinate in L and second in M. Thus the embedded denominator subgroup maps exactly to the product denominator. This is the well-definedness step for [Dolgachev §1.2](https://sites.lsa.umich.edu/idolga-new/wp-content/uploads/sites/1467/2024/08/bourbaki83.pdf#page=4)’s canonical quotient decomposition, including degenerate forms. Published [control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/IntegralLattice/Discriminant/Operations.lean#L148) passes.
The induced quotient equivalence has the expected representative formula.

The equivalence separates a dual vector into its two coordinates and reassembles them inversely. Integral pairing is componentwise for the orthogonal sum, so these maps preserve addition and integer scalars. This is the dual calculation used by [Dolgachev §1.2](https://sites.lsa.umich.edu/idolga-new/wp-content/uploads/sites/1467/2024/08/bourbaki83.pdf#page=4)’s discriminant decomposition; it needs no nondegeneracy. Published [control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/IntegralLattice/Discriminant/Operations.lean#L107) passes, [control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/IntegralLattice/Discriminant/Operations.lean#L117) passes.
The forward map splits coordinates.
The inverse map assembles coordinates.

This evaluation identity exposes the two ambient coordinates, each with its dual-membership proof. The equivalence therefore realizes the canonical dual splitting behind [Dolgachev §1.2](https://sites.lsa.umich.edu/idolga-new/wp-content/uploads/sites/1467/2024/08/bourbaki83.pdf#page=4)’s discriminant-sum formula. Subtype proofs do not change vector values, and the formula remains valid for degenerate forms. Published [control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/IntegralLattice/Discriminant/Operations.lean#L117) passes.
Reassembly recovers the original coordinate pair.

Changing B to −B preserves the condition B(x,L)⊆ℤ and leaves L unchanged. It therefore induces a canonical ℤ-linear equivalence of the same embedded dual quotients, consistent with [Nikulin §1.3](https://www.mathnet.ru/php/getFT.phtml?jrnid=im&option_lang=eng&paperid=1677&what=fullteng#page=7)’s definition. This equivalence alone concerns groups; the separate isometry theorem accounts for negated quadratic values. Published [control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/IntegralLattice/Discriminant/Operations.lean#L359) passes.
The quotient equivalence retains each ambient representative.

The quotient equivalence for form negation takes [x] to [x], using the identity equivalence of dual carriers. The original carrier is unchanged, so the formula respects its quotient relation. This is the representative identification obtained directly from [Nikulin §1.3](https://www.mathnet.ru/php/getFT.phtml?jrnid=im&option_lang=eng&paperid=1677&what=fullteng#page=7)’s discriminant-group definition. Published [control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/IntegralLattice/Discriminant/Operations.lean#L332) passes, [control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/IntegralLattice/Discriminant/Operations.lean#L469) passes.
The underlying dual vector is unchanged.
The quadratic isometry uses that same quotient representative.

Evaluating the quadratic isometry gives exactly the value of the canonical discriminant-group product equivalence. The extra quadratic-preservation proof adds no change of coordinates. This is the specified underlying map of [Nikulin §1.3](https://www.mathnet.ru/php/getFT.phtml?jrnid=im&option_lang=eng&paperid=1677&what=fullteng#page=7)’s orthogonal-sum identity, with evenness and nondegeneracy retained. Published [control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/IntegralLattice/Discriminant/Operations.lean#L283) passes.
On representatives the map gives the two component classes.

The map and its inverse both retain the ambient vector: integral pairing for −B is equivalent to integral pairing for B because ℤ is closed under negation. This is the dual identification implied by [Nikulin §1.3](https://www.mathnet.ru/php/getFT.phtml?jrnid=im&option_lang=eng&paperid=1677&what=fullteng#page=7)’s definition, with no nondegeneracy restriction. Published [control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/IntegralLattice/Discriminant/Operations.lean#L332) passes, [control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/IntegralLattice/Discriminant/Operations.lean#L338) passes.
The forward map is identity on ambient vectors.
The inverse is identity on ambient vectors.

A vector pairs integrally with L under −B exactly when it does under B, since an integer is integral together with its negative. Hence the embedded dual submodules are equal, directly from the dual definition used in [Nikulin §1.3](https://www.mathnet.ru/php/getFT.phtml?jrnid=im&option_lang=eng&paperid=1677&what=fullteng#page=7). Degenerate forms are included. Published [control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/IntegralLattice/Discriminant/Operations.lean#L338) passes.
The resulting dual identification is identity on ambient vectors.

The dual-carrier equivalence is identity on ambient vectors, and form negation leaves the original carrier unchanged. Thus it maps the embedded copy of L exactly to itself, permitting the quotient identification in [Nikulin §1.3](https://www.mathnet.ru/php/getFT.phtml?jrnid=im&option_lang=eng&paperid=1677&what=fullteng#page=7)’s discriminant construction. No finite or nondegenerate hypothesis is needed. Published [control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/IntegralLattice/Discriminant/Operations.lean#L359) passes.
The induced quotient map retains the same representative.

The inverse equivalence from Lᵛ to (−L)ᵛ changes only the membership proof, so its ambient value is the original vector. This gives the literal inverse required by the dual identification underlying [Nikulin §1.3](https://www.mathnet.ru/php/getFT.phtml?jrnid=im&option_lang=eng&paperid=1677&what=fullteng#page=7)’s discriminant construction. It is not multiplication of the vector by −1. Published [control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/IntegralLattice/Discriminant/Operations.lean#L332) passes.
The forward equivalence is also identity on ambient values.

The counit splits by the scalar map, so after any base change its kernel is generated by 1⊗ker ε. This is the identity-fiber case of [Milne, §1.e](https://www.jmilne.org/math/Books/iAG2022.pdf#page=34). [The group-kernel formula](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/HopfIdeal/Quotient/Kernel/BaseChange.lean#L168) checks the application. No flatness is needed; this is not preservation of an arbitrary linear-map kernel.
The augmentation-generated group-kernel ideal commutes with arbitrary scalar extension.

The basis identifies K⊗H with finitely supported H-valued coordinates, as in [Mathlib’s tensor basis coordinates](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/LinearAlgebra/TensorProduct/Basis.lean#L118). Applying the quotient map coordinatewise shows that a tensor lies in J_K exactly when every coordinate lies in J. [The coefficient adjunction](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/HopfIdeal/BaseChange.lean#L537) checks this criterion. The basis need not be finite.
The coefficient construction is left adjoint to extension of Hopf ideals.

This spans all coefficients of elements of I using [Mathlib’s tensor basis coordinates](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/LinearAlgebra/TensorProduct/Basis.lean#L118). Counit and antipode commute with coefficient extraction, while the tensor-square comparison proves the coideal condition. [The adjunction](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/HopfIdeal/BaseChange.lean#L537) verifies the claimed smallest ideal whose extension contains I. It does not assert that arbitrary I descends exactly.
The coefficient construction is left adjoint to extension of Hopf ideals.
The subgroup generated by a family commutes with free base change, using the coefficient Hopf ideal.

The underlying ideal is the span of all coefficients, so containment in any ideal J is precisely membership of each generator. Coefficients are those of [Mathlib’s tensor basis coordinates](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/LinearAlgebra/TensorProduct/Basis.lean#L118). [The Hopf-ideal specialization](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/HopfIdeal/BaseChange.lean#L528) checks the coercion convention; J itself need not satisfy any Hopf condition.
Hopf-ideal containment is exactly containment of all coefficients.

For a Hopf ideal J, its order is the order of the underlying ideals, so containing the coefficient ideal means containing every coefficient of every z∈I. This uses [Mathlib’s tensor basis coordinates](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/LinearAlgebra/TensorProduct/Basis.lean#L118) and the span criterion. [The scalar-extension adjunction](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/HopfIdeal/BaseChange.lean#L537) checks that no containment direction is reversed.
The coefficient construction is left adjoint to extension of Hopf ideals.

Containment of every coefficient in J is equivalent to I⊆J_K by [Mathlib’s tensor basis coordinates](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/LinearAlgebra/TensorProduct/Basis.lean#L118); hence the coefficient construction is left adjoint to scalar extension in the ideal order. [Generation under free base change](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/HopfIdeal/BaseChange.lean#L550) checks its substantive use. This is an adjunction, not a descent equivalence for all ideals.
The subgroup generated by a family commutes with free base change, using the coefficient Hopf ideal.

Tensor right exactness identifies (K⊗H)/J_K with K⊗(H/J), as in [Mathlib’s tensor-quotient comparison](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/RingTheory/TensorProduct/Quotient.lean#L86). The construction upgrades the surjective quotient map’s first-isomorphism comparison to Hopf algebras. [The quotient square](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/HopfIdeal/BaseChange.lean#L616) checks the chosen identification. This is a coordinate-algebra quotient representing a subgroup, with no flatness or normality assumption.
The canonical quotient comparison commutes with the two coordinate quotient maps.
The canonical comparison reads a quotient representative through the scalar-extended quotient map.

Quotienting K⊗H and then identifying its quotient with K⊗(H/J) is exactly id⊗q, the map underlying [Mathlib’s tensor-quotient comparison](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/RingTheory/TensorProduct/Quotient.lean#L86). [The representative formula](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/HopfIdeal/BaseChange.lean#L625) checks the composition direction. The equality is of coordinate Hopf morphisms over arbitrary commutative rings, without flatness.
The canonical comparison reads a quotient representative through the scalar-extended quotient map.

Extension and isomorphism transport send ideal spans to spans of the transported generators. The stated equality of generator images therefore identifies the Hopf ideals, consistently with [Mathlib’s tensor-quotient comparison](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/RingTheory/TensorProduct/Quotient.lean#L86). [The actual SL determinant-one comparison](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/SpecialLinear/BaseChange.lean#L90) checks the use. No finite generating set or flatness assumption is required.
The actual determinant-one quotient base-change comparison commutes with GL-to-SL coordinate maps over arbitrary commutative rings.

Inverting [Mathlib’s tensor-quotient comparison](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/RingTheory/TensorProduct/Quotient.lean#L86), then transporting the quotient along e, gives K⊗(H/J)≅H′/J′. The hypothesis explicitly identifies e(J_K) with J′. [The SL representative formula](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/SpecialLinear/BaseChange.lean#L102) checks this construction on a concrete determinant-one quotient; no equality of ambient presentations is silently assumed.
The SL comparison sends a tensor of restricted GL functions to the restriction of the GL base-change image.

Both routes send a tensor to its image under e and then its target quotient class. This is naturality of [Mathlib’s tensor-quotient comparison](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/RingTheory/TensorProduct/Quotient.lean#L86) after the supplied ideal identification. [The SL quotient-coordinate square](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/SpecialLinear/BaseChange.lean#L90) checks the intended direction. The equality compares morphisms, not merely abstractly isomorphic quotient carriers.
The actual determinant-one quotient base-change comparison commutes with GL-to-SL coordinate maps over arbitrary commutative rings.

For a K-algebra R, extending an R-valued point by s⊗h↦s·g(h) annihilates J_K exactly when g annihilates J. This is [Milne, 1.3–1.4](https://www.jmilne.org/math/Books/iAG2022.pdf#page=18) with the scalar tower explicit. [The restriction-direction criterion](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/HopfIdeal/BaseChange.lean#L830) checks the two coefficient presentations; all value algebras, including nonreduced ones, remain in scope.
Membership under restriction of a K-algebra-valued point is exactly vanishing on the original ideal.

A universally central subgroup remains central after restricting a K-algebra test to k and applying the point equivalence. This matches [Milne, 1.92](https://www.jmilne.org/math/Books/iAG2022.pdf#page=44). [Universal central-point compatibility](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/BaseChange/CentralPoint.lean#L107) checks the bridge. The statement concerns all algebra-valued points and further coefficient maps, not only rational points; arbitrary commutative base change is allowed.
The base-change point equivalence preserves and reflects universal centrality after further coefficient maps.

Coinvariants are an equalizer, so field extension commutes with them by [Mathlib’s flat equalizer comparison](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/RingTheory/Flat/Equalizer.lean#L269). Normality supplies their Hopf structure, and corestricting the extended inclusion upgrades the algebra comparison to a Hopf isomorphism. [The projection square](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/HopfIdeal/Coinvariants/HopfBaseChange.lean#L115) checks canonicity. No smoothness, reducedness or finite-type hypothesis is imposed.
The Hopf coinvariant comparison commutes with quotient coordinate inclusions.
The inverse Hopf comparison is exactly the inverse flat equalizer comparison.

The Hopf comparison uses the underlying map of [Mathlib’s flat equalizer comparison](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/RingTheory/Flat/Equalizer.lean#L269); only its bundled structure is strengthened. [The inverse formula](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/HopfIdeal/Coinvariants/HopfBaseChange.lean#L105) and [ambient inclusion formula](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/HopfIdeal/Coinvariants/BaseChange.lean#L123) check that no alternate coinvariant carrier or noncanonical identification is introduced.
The inverse Hopf comparison is exactly the inverse flat equalizer comparison.
The coinvariant comparison includes into the ambient algebra as the ordinary tensor of the inclusion.

After inclusion in K⊗H, both maps send an extended coinvariant to the same ambient tensor. This is the canonical equalizer map of [Mathlib’s flat equalizer comparison](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/RingTheory/Flat/Equalizer.lean#L269). [The inverse comparison square](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/HopfIdeal/Coinvariants/HopfBaseChange.lean#L128) checks orientation: coordinate inclusions correspond contravariantly to quotient projections, not to subgroup inclusions.
The inverse coinvariant comparison also commutes with the coordinate inclusion.

The two quotient projections differ by the canonical Hopf isomorphism, so their scheme-theoretic kernel ideals agree, consistent with [Milne, §1.e](https://www.jmilne.org/math/Books/iAG2022.pdf#page=34). [The general kernel base-change identity](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/HopfIdeal/Quotient/Kernel/BaseChange.lean#L168) checks its interpretation. These are augmentation-generated group-kernel ideals, not ordinary kernels of the injective coinvariant coordinate maps.
The augmentation-generated group-kernel ideal commutes with arbitrary scalar extension.

The kernel comparison and base-change identity turn the left equality into equality of two extended Hopf ideals; faithful flatness of a field extension reflects it. This follows the exactness convention in [Milne, §1.e](https://www.jmilne.org/math/Books/iAG2022.pdf#page=34). [Reflection of ideal equality](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/HopfIdeal/BaseChange.lean#L266) checks descent. It transports an exactness assertion, rather than proving that assertion unconditionally.
Faithfully flat extension reflects equality of Hopf ideals.
The two identified quotient projections have the same augmentation-generated kernel ideal.

For every k-algebra A, the map A→K⊗A is injective for a field extension. Normality upstairs forces each conjugate to annihilate I after this map, hence already in A, as in [Milne, proof of Proposition 5.18](https://www.jmilne.org/math/Books/iAG2022.pdf#page=114). [The preservation-and-reflection criterion](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/HopfIdeal/Normal/Descent.lean#L64) checks the result; rational-point normality alone would not suffice.
Preservation and reflection combine to normality iff normality after any field extension.

The group-kernel ideal is generated by f(H⁺), as in [Milne, §1.e](https://www.jmilne.org/math/Books/iAG2022.pdf#page=34). Base change preserves H⁺ and composition of ideal extension, giving the stated equality over arbitrary commutative rings. [The identity-fiber representative formula](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/HopfIdeal/Quotient/Kernel/BaseChange.lean#L92) checks the convention. No flatness is required, unlike base change of an arbitrary ordinary algebra kernel.
The group-kernel coordinate quotient is the identity fiber, sending [x] to x⊗1.
The identity-section ideal base-changes to the augmentation ideal without flatness.

The set of continuous maps sending compact K into open U is open in the compact-open topology. These are precisely its generating subbasic sets M(K,U). Compactness of K and openness of U are explicit; no Hausdorff or local-compactness assumption on either ambient space is needed. [Hatcher §2](https://pi.math.cornell.edu/~hatcher/AT/ATapp.pdf); [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Topology/CompactOpen.lean#L59).

A neighborhood of f contains a finite intersection of compact-open subbasic sets, each containing f. The finite set S records the compact/open pairs, and MapsTo expresses both membership of f and the intersection constraint on g. This is the usual neighborhood basis of a topology generated by a subbasis. [Hatcher §2](https://pi.math.cornell.edu/~hatcher/AT/ATapp.pdf); [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Topology/CompactOpen.lean#L105).

Convergence to g in the compact-open topology means eventual membership in every subbasic neighborhood M(K,U) of g. The displayed MapsTo conditions express exactly that criterion for an arbitrary filter. Finite intersections require no extra hypothesis because filters are closed under finite intersections. [Hatcher §2](https://pi.math.cornell.edu/~hatcher/AT/ATapp.pdf); [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Topology/CompactOpen.lean#L87).

Postcomposition by a fixed continuous g is continuous between compact-open mapping spaces. The inverse image of M(K,U) is M(K,g⁻¹(U)); continuity of g makes that target set open. The unchanged compact set K supplies the required subbasic neighborhood without local compactness assumptions. [Hatcher §2](https://pi.math.cornell.edu/~hatcher/AT/ATapp.pdf); [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Topology/CompactOpen.lean#L139).

Precomposition by a fixed continuous f is continuous in the compact-open topologies. The inverse image of M(K,U) is M(f(K),U), and f(K) is compact by continuity. Thus the statement correctly needs neither properness of f nor local compactness of its source or target. [Hatcher §2](https://pi.math.cornell.edu/~hatcher/AT/ATapp.pdf); [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Topology/CompactOpen.lean#L164).

An injective target map g makes postcomposition injective: equality g∘f₁=g∘f₂ cancels pointwise to f₁=f₂. The bundled maps carry their required continuity, but the cancellation itself is set-theoretic. No nonemptiness of the source or additional separation property is required. [Hatcher §2](https://pi.math.cornell.edu/~hatcher/AT/ATapp.pdf); [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Topology/CompactOpen.lean#L144).

If Y has the topology induced by g into Z, postcomposition similarly induces the compact-open topology on C(X,Y). Every open target subset is a preimage under g, so the compact-open generators correspond exactly. The hypothesis is topology induction; injectivity is separately needed for an embedding. [Hatcher §2](https://pi.math.cornell.edu/~hatcher/AT/ATapp.pdf); [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Topology/CompactOpen.lean#L150).

Joint continuity of (x,y)↦f(x)(y) implies continuity of x↦f(x) into the compact-open mapping space. This is the currying direction of Hatcher A.14(b), valid for arbitrary topological spaces. The source constructs the associated bundled curry, whose continuity is already part of its type. [Hatcher §2](https://pi.math.cornell.edu/~hatcher/AT/ATapp.pdf); [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Topology/CompactOpen.lean#L440).

Currying sends a continuous map on X×Y to the continuous family x↦(y↦f(x,y)) in C(Y,Z). Hatcher A.14(b) ensures this construction for arbitrary spaces. The additional local-compactness condition mentioned in the prose concerns continuity of the curry operator between mapping spaces, not existence of each bundled curried map. [Hatcher §2](https://pi.math.cornell.edu/~hatcher/AT/ATapp.pdf); [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Topology/CompactOpen.lean#L430).

Uncurrying evaluates the family f at the variable point: (x,y)↦f(x)(y). The hypothesis that Y is locally compact makes evaluation jointly continuous, yielding the bundled map on X×Y. This is Hatcher A.14(c), with no additional local compactness or Hausdorff condition on X or Z. [Hatcher §2](https://pi.math.cornell.edu/~hatcher/AT/ATapp.pdf); [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Topology/CompactOpen.lean#L466).

The uncurrying operator is continuous when both X and Y are locally compact. Its fully evaluated form is continuous by evaluating first at x and then at y; currying that jointly continuous expression gives the result. This directly applies Hatcher A.14 repeatedly without requiring Hausdorffness of either factor. [Hatcher §2](https://pi.math.cornell.edu/~hatcher/AT/ATapp.pdf); [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Topology/CompactOpen.lean#L471).

For a fixed x, evaluation f↦f(x) is continuous in the compact-open topology. Its inverse image of an open U is M({x},U), and a singleton is compact in any space. Thus the instance correctly imposes no local compactness or separation assumption on X. [Hatcher §2](https://pi.math.cornell.edu/~hatcher/AT/ATapp.pdf); [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Topology/CompactOpen.lean#L251).

Joint evaluation is continuous under LocallyCompactPair X Y: around f(x), that class supplies a compact neighborhood K of x with f(K) inside the chosen target neighborhood. Then M(K,U)×K controls evaluation. This is exactly Hatcher A.14(a)’s argument, generalized to the stated pair condition. [Hatcher §2](https://pi.math.cornell.edu/~hatcher/AT/ATapp.pdf); [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Topology/CompactOpen.lean#L244).

If Y is T₀, two distinct continuous maps differ at some x, and a target open set distinguishes their values there. Fixed-point evaluation pulls that distinction back to a compact-open set. Hence C(X,Y) is T₀ for arbitrary X, including an empty source. [Hatcher §2](https://pi.math.cornell.edu/~hatcher/AT/ATapp.pdf); [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Topology/CompactOpen.lean#L279).

A Hausdorff target makes the compact-open mapping space Hausdorff: distinct maps differ at a point, whose two values have disjoint open neighborhoods. Their fixed-point evaluation preimages give disjoint neighborhoods of the maps. This argument works for arbitrary X and requires neither compactness nor local compactness of X. [Hatcher §2](https://pi.math.cornell.edu/~hatcher/AT/ATapp.pdf); [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Topology/CompactOpen.lean#L293).

If f sends compact K into open U, every sufficiently nearby continuous map does so as well. The neighborhood filter statement says precisely that f belongs to the open subbasic set M(K,U). It is a compact-open stability statement for the whole K, with no metric or quantitative margin assumed. [Hatcher §2](https://pi.math.cornell.edu/~hatcher/AT/ATapp.pdf); [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Topology/CompactOpen.lean#L65).

The assignment (x,f)↦(y↦(x,f(y))) is continuous between the stated product and compact-open spaces. For compact K, the tube lemma around {x}×f(K) supplies uniform product neighborhoods controlling every y∈K. Thus no local compactness assumption on Y is needed for this particular family construction. [Hatcher §2](https://pi.math.cornell.edu/~hatcher/AT/ATapp.pdf); [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Topology/CompactOpen.lean#L188).

A map g:Y×X→Z is continuous if its pullback along id_Y×f is continuous, when f is quotient and Y is locally compact. Hatcher A.17 states that product quotient property. The Lean proof swaps factors, descends a curried family through f, and uncurries it. [Hatcher §2](https://pi.math.cornell.edu/~hatcher/AT/ATapp.pdf); [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Topology/CompactOpen.lean#L600).

Restriction bundles the function on the subset s with its subspace topology, evaluating an element of s by its ambient value under f. Continuity follows by composing with the subspace inclusion. The construction works for every subset, so no openness, closedness or nonemptiness assumption on s is missing. [Wendl §3](https://www.math.hu-berlin.de/~wendl/Sommer2026/Topologie1/lecturenotes.pdf); [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Topology/ContinuousMap/Basic.lean#L280).

For s⊆t, the inclusion sends each element of s to the same underlying point regarded as an element of t. Both subsets carry their subspace topologies, making this map continuous. The source’s composition and ambient-inclusion identities verify the expected behavior of nested subset inclusions. [Wendl §3](https://www.math.hu-berlin.de/~wendl/Sommer2026/Topologie1/lecturenotes.pdf); [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Topology/ContinuousMap/Basic.lean#L421).

A bundled continuous semilinear map is continuous as an ordinary function. The theorem returns the continuity proof stored in the bundle. It makes no claim that an arbitrary semilinear map is automatically continuous. Compared with [the reference](https://www.math.ttu.edu/~rgelca/FUNCTANAL.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Topology/Algebra/Module/ContinuousLinearMap/Basic.lean#L143).

Bundled continuous semilinear maps satisfy the corresponding map class: they preserve addition, transport scalars through σ, and are continuous. The instance exposes exactly those three properties from the existing bundle. Compared with [the reference](https://www.math.ttu.edu/~rgelca/FUNCTANAL.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Topology/Algebra/Module/ContinuousLinearMap/Basic.lean#L129).

Two continuous semilinear maps with the same scalar transport are equal when they agree at every input. Continuity and semilinearity proofs do not create different maps with identical values. Compared with [the reference](https://math.ucdavis.edu/~hunter/book/ch5.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Topology/Algebra/Module/ContinuousLinearMap/Basic.lean#L184).

The function coercion for a continuous semilinear map returns its underlying semilinear function and is injective on bundles. This supports the usual identification of operators by their values. Compared with [the reference](https://math.ucdavis.edu/~hunter/book/ch5.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Topology/Algebra/Module/ContinuousLinearMap/Basic.lean#L125).

A codomain scalar action scales continuous semilinear maps pointwise when it distributes over addition, commutes with the target module action, and is continuous for each fixed scalar. These hypotheses ensure the scaled map remains semilinear and continuous. Compared with [the reference](https://math.ucdavis.edu/~hunter/book/ch5.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Topology/Algebra/Module/ContinuousLinearMap/Basic.lean#L291).

Addition of continuous semilinear maps evaluates pointwise: (f+g)(x)=f(x)+g(x). Continuous addition in the target ensures this pointwise sum is continuous, and the common scalar transport preserves semilinearity. Compared with [the reference](https://math.ucdavis.edu/~hunter/book/ch5.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Topology/Algebra/Module/ContinuousLinearMap/Basic.lean#L419).

Negating a continuous semilinear map negates its value at each input. The actual ring, additive-group and topological-additive-group assumptions make the negated map semilinear and continuous. Compared with [the reference](https://math.ucdavis.edu/~hunter/book/ch5.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Topology/Algebra/Module/ContinuousLinearMap/Basic.lean#L821).

The scalar action on continuous semilinear maps has the expected evaluation rule, (c • f)(x)=c • f(x). It uses the same distributive, commuting and fixed-scalar continuity assumptions as the underlying scalar-action construction. Compared with [the reference](https://math.ucdavis.edu/~hunter/book/ch5.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Topology/Algebra/Module/ContinuousLinearMap/Basic.lean#L294).

The zero continuous semilinear map evaluates to the target zero at every input. The zero function is continuous for arbitrary topologies and is semilinear under the module zero laws. Compared with [the reference](https://math.ucdavis.edu/~hunter/book/ch5.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Topology/Algebra/Module/ContinuousLinearMap/Basic.lean#L328).

Continuous maps into an additive commutative monoid with continuous addition form an additive commutative monoid under pointwise operations. The generated additive instance retains the zero function, pointwise sum and natural repeated sums. Compared with [the reference](https://devitoernesto.github.io/pub_files/rkhs_universal.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Topology/ContinuousMap/Algebra.lean#L271).

A fixed-scalar continuous action on the target induces scalar multiplication of continuous maps by postcomposition. Its underlying function is x↦c • f(x). No algebraic laws beyond the given scalar operation are required. Compared with [the reference](https://devitoernesto.github.io/pub_files/rkhs_universal.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Topology/ContinuousMap/Algebra.lean#L524).

A bundled continuous map coerces injectively to its underlying function. Continuity proofs do not affect equality, so this faithfully implements continuous maps as functions with a continuity property. Compared with [the reference](https://www.math.ttu.edu/~rgelca/FUNCTANAL.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Topology/ContinuousMap/Defs.lean#L78).

Bounded continuous functions are closed under pointwise scalar multiplication for an IsBoundedSMul action. The defining Lipschitz bound supplies continuity and multiplies a pairwise image-distance bound by dist(c,0), giving the required bounded image. Compared with [the reference](https://math.ucdavis.edu/~hunter/book/ch5.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Topology/ContinuousMap/Bounded/Basic.lean#L692).

The zero bounded continuous function is the constant function with value zero. It is continuous and its image has pairwise distance zero, so no compactness of the domain is needed. Compared with [the reference](https://devitoernesto.github.io/pub_files/rkhs_universal.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Topology/ContinuousMap/Bounded/Basic.lean#L474).

Coercing a sum of functions vanishing at infinity gives their pointwise sum. Continuous target addition and 0+0=0 ensure that the sum remains continuous and tends to zero along the cocompact filter. Compared with [the reference](https://devitoernesto.github.io/pub_files/rkhs_universal.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Topology/ContinuousMap/ZeroAtInfty.lean#L198).

The zero element of C₀ is the literal constant zero function after coercion. The identity is definitional and agrees with the usual zero of a function space. Compared with [the reference](https://devitoernesto.github.io/pub_files/rkhs_universal.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Topology/ContinuousMap/ZeroAtInfty.lean#L170).

Functions in C₀ are equal when they agree at every point. Their continuity and vanishing-at-infinity proofs do not add observable data. No Hausdorff assumption is needed for this extensional equality. Compared with [the reference](https://devitoernesto.github.io/pub_files/rkhs_universal.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Topology/ContinuousMap/ZeroAtInfty.lean#L102).

Pointwise addition and the zero function make C₀ an AddZeroClass when its target has continuous addition and an AddZeroClass structure. Both zero-identity laws transfer from the target. Compared with [the reference](https://devitoernesto.github.io/pub_files/rkhs_universal.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Topology/ContinuousMap/ZeroAtInfty.lean#L204).

The constant zero continuous function vanishes at infinity, so it defines the zero element of C₀ for every topological domain and every target with a topology and zero. Compared with [the reference](https://devitoernesto.github.io/pub_files/rkhs_universal.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Topology/ContinuousMap/ZeroAtInfty.lean#L163).

The C₀ bundle has an injective coercion to its underlying function. Continuity and the cocompact zero-limit property are proof fields, so the bundle carries exactly the expected function data. Compared with [the reference](https://devitoernesto.github.io/pub_files/rkhs_universal.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Topology/ContinuousMap/ZeroAtInfty.lean#L80).
